animal.name: wood frog
animal.look: small North American wood frog, warm brown skin, a dark mask stripe through its golden eyes, cream belly

post.title: This frog freezes solid… and survives 🐸❄️
post.description:
Send this to someone who needs a reminder that winter ends.

The wood frog lets up to about two-thirds of its body water freeze. Its heart stops, and glucose from its liver protects its cells until spring.
post.pinned_comment: Would you rather freeze like this frog or hibernate like a bear? 👇

scenes.pose: lying motionless under fallen leaves, eyes closed, covered in ice crystals
scenes.narration: This little frog can freeze solid… and still survive.

scenes.pose: sitting on the ground, eyes half closed
scenes.narration: When winter arrives in the northern forests, most animals run away, or hide deep underground. The wood frog does something else. It simply lets the cold take it.
As ice begins to form, its liver floods its body with glucose. This sugar works like a natural antifreeze, protecting the cells that keep it alive.

scenes.pose: frozen solid, eyes closed, lying flat
scenes.narration: Then its heart stops. It stops breathing. Up to two-thirds of the water in its body turns to ice.

scenes.pose: frozen solid, eyes closed, lying flat
scenes.narration: For weeks, sometimes for months, it lies frozen under the snow. No heartbeat. No breath. Not dead. Just waiting for spring.
And when the ground finally warms, the ice melts away. Its heart flickers back to life. It takes a breath. And it opens its eyes.
Nature doesn't always escape the impossible. Sometimes… it survives it.
